description: Recompute an invoice exactly and report where it disagrees with itself. Quantity times unit price is an exact decimal product. Rounding happens only where the stated policy says: per line, or once on the whole invoice. Those give different totals, so the difference between the two policies is published rather than one being assumed correct. Also reports a figure with more decimal places than its currency has, and a discount larger than its line. Pay 220000 atomic USDC on Base via exact x402. MCP does not pay; it provides a challenge handoff.

invoice.description: The invoice to recompute. Nothing is fetched and no system is connected, so the data supplied is the whole input.

currency.description: The three-letter code, which decides how many decimal places a figure may carry.

discount.description: Deducted from this line before tax. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

line_total.description: The declared line total, compared against the computed one. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

quantity.description: How many. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

tax_amount.description: The declared line tax, compared against the computed one. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

tax_rate.description: As a percentage, so 10 means ten per cent. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

unit_price.description: Price for one. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

subtotal.description: The declared subtotal. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

tax_total.description: The declared tax total. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

total.description: The declared total. A decimal string is preferred, because a JSON number cannot hold most two-place decimals exactly and the digits may already differ from what was written by the time they arrive. A number is accepted and that risk is reported.

policy.description: The accounting policy the invoice was built under. These change the answer, so they are stated rather than assumed.

minor_units.description: Decimal places per currency code, overriding the published table. Two is the default because most currencies have two.

round_per_line.description: Round each line, or sum exactly and round once. Defaults to per line.

rounding.description: How a figure is rounded. Required rather than defaulted in spirit: half-up and half-even disagree on every price ending in 5, so the mode is an accounting policy and is published in the response. Defaults to half_up when omitted.

tax_inclusive.description: Whether unit prices already include tax. Inclusive and exclusive are different formulas that do not round to the same figure. Defaults to false.

name: invoice_arithmetic_audit

arithmetic_sound.description: True only when every declared figure matched the computed one and every figure fitted the currency.

complete.description: Whether everything supplied was examined. False means part of it was not, which is a different problem from something that is wrong.

finding_count.description: The true total, even when the listing is bounded.

lines.description: Per line: exact and rounded net and tax, so every step is checkable.

passed.description: The same verdict under the name shared across the caller-supplied families.

request_id.description: Delivery request identifier; also returned in x-foundry-request-id.

rounding_policy_difference.description: What choosing per-line rounding over whole-invoice rounding costs on this invoice.

subtotal_exact_unrounded.description: The sum before any rounding, so the effect of the policy is visible.

title: Invoice Arithmetic Audit
